hero.title: Blockchain for PHP developers: a safe bridge with Node.js
hero.subtitle: Keep your PHP application, add a small Node.js chain service, a tiny payment contract and signed webhooks, and learn to handle money exactly and calmly. Every task is checked and explained.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can design and build a careful blockchain integration for an existing PHP application.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). Short tests inside the lessons give instant feedback.
Complete the checkout design and the final assessment.

faq.q: Does the platform run PHP or Node.js?
faq.a: No. The labs check your designs, calculations and writing. You run the code in your own environment on a test network.
They were written and reviewed by hand but not executed by the platform. Test them in your own environment with PHP 8.1 or newer before relying on them.

faq.q: Can I take real payments after this?
faq.a: Not without a security review and legal and tax advice for your country. This is education, and a regulated payment provider may suit a real shop better.

activities.title: Convert a price to token base units
activities.objective: Convert a rupee price into a stablecoin amount and the exact whole number the contract needs, and decide whether a payment is acceptable.
activities.scenario: An order costs 4,999 rupees. One stablecoin unit is 83.5 rupees and the token has 6 decimals. A customer paid 59,600,000 base units. Your shop accepts up to 0.5% under the price. (A teaching model.)
steps: In B7 work out the price in tokens, rounded to 2 decimals.
In B8 work out the price in base units: B7 times 10 to the power of the decimals, rounded to a whole number.
In B9 work out the lowest amount you will accept: B8 times (100 minus the tolerance) over 100, rounded.
In B10 show Accept if the amount paid (B6) is at least B9, otherwise Underpaid.
In B11 work out how much was overpaid, zero if nothing.

checks.label: B7 is the price in tokens
checks.hint: =ROUND(B2/B3,2)

checks.label: B8 is the price in base units
checks.hint: =ROUND(B7*POWER(10,B4),0)
checks.explain: Multiply by 10 to the decimals and round.

checks.label: B9 is the lowest accepted
B10 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B6>=B9,"Accept","Underpaid")
checks.explain: Compare the payment with the lowest accepted.

checks.label: B11 is the overpayment

activities.title: How reliable is your webhook?
activities.objective: Calculate how retries reduce the chance of losing a notification.
activities.scenario: Your PHP server is unreachable half the time during a bad hour. The Node service retries 4 times. (A teaching model.)
steps: In B7 work out the chance that all attempts fail: the failure chance (as a fraction) to the power of the attempts.
In B8 work out the chance that at least one attempt succeeds.
In B9 work out how many of the orders are expected to lose their notification.
In B10 show Add more attempts if B7 is 0.01 or more, otherwise Reliable enough.
In B11 show the success chance as a percentage.

checks.label: B7 is the all-fail chance
checks.hint: =POWER(B2/100,B3)
checks.explain: The fraction to the power of the attempts.

checks.label: B8 is the success chance
checks.hint: Try the formula =1-B7 here.

checks.label: B9 is the expected loss
B10 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B7<0.01,"Reliable enough","Add more attempts")

checks.label: B11 is the percentage

activities.title: How many confirmations, and how long?
activities.objective: Balance waiting time against reorganisation risk by order value.
activities.scenario: Blocks arrive every 12 seconds. Small orders wait 2 confirmations and large orders wait 12. An order is large above 10,000 rupees. (A teaching model.)
steps: In B7 work out the wait for small orders in seconds.
In B8 work out the wait for large orders in seconds.
In B9 work out the large-order wait in minutes.
In B10 work out how many extra seconds large orders wait.
In B11 show Use 12 confirmations if the order value (B5) is above the threshold (B6), otherwise Use 2 confirmations.

checks.label: B7 is the small wait
B8 is the large wait
B9 is the wait in minutes
B10 is the extra wait
B11 is the policy
checks.hint: =IF(B5>B6,"Use 12 confirmations","Use 2 confirmations")
